messages:
Incidents Bot: :rotating_light: AUTOALERT — region=us-east-1 — increased 5xx rate observed for hosted API and Dedicated pools. Metrics: >5% 5xx on /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings over the last 3m. Error signature shows token fetch/metadata timeouts. Paging on-call: @Alice Nguyen

Alice Nguyen: taking the page. starting triage — pulling traces, auth logs, error samples.

Maria SRE: quick summary from traces: most failures are upstream auth failures while fetching credentials from IMDS (169.254.169.254). Timeouts and occasional TCP RST seen from control plane hosts across multiple AZs.

Dave (ops): running a quick probe from control plane host (k8s pod):
```
curl -sS -m 2 http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ || echo "IMDS_ERR:$?"
# got blank response in some attempts, others timed out (28)
```

Samir Patel: pushing temporary routing override to divert non-critical traffic away from us-east-1 to us-west-2. Will flag tenant-level routing for best-effort failover. Applying now.

Irene Cole: starting mitigation runbook steps: 1) increase local token cache TTL for Dedicated pools 2) enable cached-cred fallback for control-plane auth 3) raise client-side retry/backoff on STS calls.

Alice Nguyen: checklist updated in thread. Noting customer impact and next steps. Contacting support/eng-sre channel for deeper infra checks.

Incidents Bot: Created AWS case #CASE-7890123 and attached initial logs. ETA from AWS: probing IMDS service in us-east-1.

Maria SRE: observing effects from routing override — error rate for hosted API dropped from ~8.2% -> ~3.1% for traffic routed to us-west-2. Dedicated pools in us-east-1 still showing ~10-12% failures for some customers using local instances.

Dave (ops): temporarily disabling a high-frequency observability exporter to the third-party vendor for us-east-1 control-plane (reduces extra egress load). Command ran: `kubectl patch cm observability-config -n controlplane --type merge -p '{"data":{"export_rate":"0.1"}}'`

Samir Patel: increased token-refresh retry attempts 3->6 with exponential backoff + jitter on the auth client. Deployed a canary to 5 pods, observed successful reduction of auth fail rate on retries.

Alice Nguyen: impact assessment: approx 8% of hosted API requests experienced transient 5xx during peak; Dedicated pools saw higher error ratios (10-15%) for a subset of customers whose pods rely on IMDS for short-lived creds. No persisted data loss. Business impact: degraded latency and failed requests for some paying customers; recommend incident communication to affected customers.

Maria SRE: AWS update (from case): investigating elevated throttling at IMDS layer affecting metadata responses in us-east-1; they are applying mitigation in infra, ETA ~18m.

Irene Cole: preparing handoff notes for night shift. Current mitigations in place: routing override, cached-cred TTL increased, client retry tuning, reduced observability egress. Next steps: monitor error rate, keep AWS case open, gather auth logs for postmortem, prepare customer comms draft (CS owns).

Alice Nguyen: handing off to @Irene Cole for continued monitoring (taking over pager at 20:40 UTC). Handoff notes pinned: what we changed, how to rollback routing override if it causes issues, where to find canary logs, AWS case ID.

Irene Cole: acknowledged. Will maintain watch for 2h and escalate if 5xx >5% or if AWS ETA slips.

Dave (ops): reminder — do not rotate credentials while fallback cache is active. We will coordinate any key ops in this thread.

Alice Nguyen: leaving the thread in monitoring state. Action items: 1) CS to prepare customer notification, 2) Infra to collect full STS/IMDS traces for postmortem, 3) Investigate longer-term decoupling from IMDS for Dedicated pool token refresh.

Incidents Bot: :white_check_mark: Incident moved to 'monitoring' — no ongoing immediate action required by page owner.

Irene Cole: closing active pager handoff. Will update if AWS confirms full recovery or if we see regression.
